title: Relational data modelling

children.title: Normal forms and decomposition
children.brief: Develop systematic ways to justify a relational design from stated dependencies. The parent establishes the shop's normalisation, the meaning of 3NF and BCNF, a simple lossless split, and the distinction between reconstruction and preserving rules. Build on that to find candidate keys using attribute closure, analyse overlapping keys, compare dependency-preserving 3NF synthesis with BCNF decomposition, and reason about multivalued and join dependencies where independent sets produce redundancy even in BCNF. Explain 4NF and the practical question behind 5NF with explicit business rules and counterexamples. The outcome is being able to test and defend difficult decompositions, rather than choosing a normal form by its number.

children.title: Trees and graphs in relational databases
children.brief: Choose and assess representations for hierarchical and graph data. The parent establishes self-referencing roles, adjacency lists, multiple-parent relationships and the limits of a foreign key. Develop the trade-offs among adjacency lists, closure tables, materialised paths and nested sets by following ancestor searches, subtree moves and deletions on the same proposed category example. Distinguish a general graph from a tree and explain the additional invariants and stored redundancy each representation introduces. Connect enforcement, recursive SQL and measured performance to their neighbours rather than assuming the representation alone guarantees them.
